explanation:
In the mirror, left and right appear reversed.

---

- **映る（うつる）** — to be reflected, to appear (in a surface); intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 映す(うつす). Describes an image being cast onto a reflective surface. [JLPT N3]

I want a mirror that can show my whole body.

---

- **映す（うつす）** — to reflect, to project, to show (an image); transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 映る(うつる). The causative form 映せる expresses "can reflect / is able to show." [JLPT N2]

Because of the heavy rain, even the floor of the house was submerged in water.

---

- **つかる（漬かる／浸かる）** — to be soaked, to be submerged; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: つける(つける). Indicates the subject becomes immersed in liquid. [JLPT N2]

When stains are hard to remove, it is effective to soak them in detergent solution for a while.

---

- **つける（漬ける／浸ける）** — to soak, to immerse; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: つかる(つかる). The 〜ておくと construction means "if you do X in advance, it will be good." [JLPT N2]

A boat is floating on the pond.

---

- **浮かぶ（浮ぶ）** — to float, to appear (in one's mind); intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 浮かべる(うかべる). Describes an object resting on the surface of liquid. [JLPT N2]

I floated a toy boat on the pond and played.

---

- **浮かべる（浮べる）** — to float (something), to cause to float; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 浮かぶ(うかぶ). Also used figuratively: 笑顔を浮かべる (put on a smile). [JLPT N2]

A one-yen coin floats on water.

---

- **浮く（うく）** — to float; intransitive verb (自動詞). Focuses on buoyancy (not sinking). Note: also means "to feel out of place" or "to be unfaithful" in other contexts. [JLPT N2]

Japan's "Ama" (women divers) can dive into the sea for long periods to catch shellfish and fish.

---

- **潜る（潜る／くぐる・もぐる）** — to dive, to go under; intransitive verb (自動詞). Reading is もぐる when diving into water; くぐる when passing under something. Counterpart: 潜める is rare; usually expressed with other verbs. [JLPT N2]

The frog leapt high off the ground and disappeared into the grass.

---

- **跳ねる（はねる）** — to jump, to leap, to bounce; intransitive verb (自動詞). Also means "to kick up" (mud splashing) or "to malfunction" (machinery going haywire). [JLPT N2]

Carry a backpack on one's back.

---

- **背負う（せおう）** — to carry on one's back, to bear (responsibility); transitive verb (他動詞). In casual speech, pronounced 「しょう」. Note: Chinese false friend — does not mean "to betray" like 背負 in Chinese. [JLPT N2]

The child ran after their mother.

---

- **追う（おう）** — to chase, to pursue, to follow; transitive verb (他動詞). Can be used literally (chasing someone) or figuratively (pursuing a dream/goal). Counterpart: 追われる(おわれる) is passive.
- **〜の後を追う** — to follow after someone. [JLPT N2]

I chased the criminal but they got away.

---

- **追いかける（追掛ける）** — to chase after, to pursue; transitive verb (他動詞), derived from 追う + かける (continuous/iterative action). The 〜たが、〜てしまった pattern expresses a failed attempt with regret. [JLPT N2]

He is fast, so even if I chase him now, I probably won't catch up.

---

- **追いつく（追いつく／追付く）** — to catch up (with); intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 追い（overtake）+ つく（reach/arrive). Note the negative form 追いつかない expresses inability. [JLPT N2]

I caught up with the runner ahead, but couldn't overtake them.

---

- **追い越す（追い越す／追いこす）** — to overtake, to pass; transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 追い + 越す (cross over/surpass). The sentence contrasts 追いつく (catch up) with 追い越す (overtake). [JLPT N2]

I turned around when someone called my name.

---

- **振り向く（振り向く／ふりむく）** — to turn around (to look back); intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 振り（turn）+ 向く（face toward). Also used figuratively: attention being directed toward something. [JLPT N2]

I caught a cicada in the park.

---

- **捕る（とる）** — to catch (an animal, insect, or fish); transitive verb (他動詞). Note: three homophones distinguished by kanji — 捕る (catch living things), 採る (gather plants/minerals/data), 執る (conduct a ceremony/hold a position). [JLPT N2]

She picked up the book on the desk.

---

- **取り上げる（取り上げる）** — to pick up, to take away, to adopt (a topic); transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 取り（take）+ 上げる（raise). Multiple meanings: physically lift something, confiscate, or address a subject. [JLPT N2]

Bring in the laundry.

---

- **取り入れる（取り入れる）** — to take in, to bring in, to adopt (ideas/customs); transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 取り（take）+ 入れる（put in). Commonly used for harvesting crops or bringing in laundry from outside. [JLPT N2]

I sharpened a pencil with a knife.

---

- **削る（けずる）** — to shave off, to削る (whittle, scrape, pare down); transitive verb (他動詞). Used for reducing amounts (budget cuts) or physically shaving material. [JLPT N2]

Stack old magazines and tie them with string.

---

- **縛る（しばる）** — to tie, to bind, to restrict; transitive verb (他動詞). Also used figuratively: rules that bind/restrict people. Counterpart: 縛られる(しばられる) is passive. [JLPT N2]

Wring out a towel soaked in water.

---

- **絞る（しぼる）** — to wring out, to squeeze; transitive verb (他動詞). Also written as 搾る when squeezing juice from fruit. Related: 絞り込む (narrow down). Counterpart: 絞られる(しぼられる). [JLPT N2]

The Earth revolves around the Sun.

---

- **回る（まわる）** — to rotate, to revolve, to go around; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 回す(まわす). Used for physical rotation, visiting multiple places, or something being distributed. [JLPT N2]

Turn the doorknob to open the door.

---

- **回す（まわす）** — to turn, to rotate (something); transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 回る(まわる). Also means to operate a machine, or send something around to people. [JLPT N2]

Speaking while pausing between each word.

---

- **区切る（くぎる）** — to separate into sections, to divide, to pause (in speech); transitive verb (他動詞). Used for marking boundaries (physical or temporal). Compound of 区（section）+ 切る（cut). [JLPT N2]

Cross one's {legs / arms / shoulders}.

---

- **組む（くむ）** — to assemble, to pair up, to cross/interlock (body parts); intransitive verb (自動詞). In this frame, refers to crossing limbs. Also: to team up, to combine. [JLPT N2]

I assembled the parts and made a machine.

---

- **組み立てる（組み立てる）** — to assemble, to construct, to organize (an argument); transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 組み（combine）+ 立てる（set up). Used for furniture, machines, or logical structures. [JLPT N2]

A new player joined the team.

---

- **加わる（くわわる）** — to be added, to join; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 加える(くわえる). Note: the particle can be に (join a group) or と (add to a sum). [JLPT N2]

If you add 8 to 3, it becomes 11.

---

- **加える（くわえる）** — to add; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 加わる(くわわる). Used in math, adding ingredients, or adding items to a set. [JLPT N2]

The scarf I'm giving to my lover is finally finished.

---

- **仕上がる（仕上がる）** — to be completed, to be finished; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 仕上げる(しあげる). Compound: 仕（do) + 上がる（rise up to completion). Implies the final stage of a process. [JLPT N2]

"Please finish this work by the end of the month."

---

- **仕上げる（仕上げる）** — to complete, to finish (something); transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 仕上がる(しあがる). Implies bringing something to its final polished state, not just "doing" it. [JLPT N2]

When I happened to pass by a ramen shop, there was a large crowd of people lining up.

---

- **通り掛かる（通り掛かる）** — to happen to pass by; intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 通り（pass through）+ 掛かる（be in the process of). The 〜掛かる suffix indicates an incidental/intermediate state. [JLPT N2]

Honeybees are buzzing about, flying all over.

---

- **飛び回る（飛び回る）** — to fly around (restlessly), to bustle about; intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 飛び（fly）+ 回る（go around). The 〜回る suffix adds the nuance of repeated or energetic action in multiple directions. The onomatopoeia ぶんぶん mimics buzzing. [JLPT N2]

The Earth orbits around the Sun.

---

- **巡る（めぐる）** — to go around, to circulate, to revolve; intransitive verb (自動詞). Similar to 回る but with a more literary/formal tone, often used for seasons, blood circulation, or cosmic motion. [JLPT N2]

I'm taking medicine to make up for nutritional deficiency.

---

- **補う（おぎなう）** — to supplement, to make up for, to compensate; transitive verb (他動詞). Used for filling a gap (nutrition, finances, knowledge, experience). Kango verb with a formal register. [JLPT N2]

To guard against thieves, I installed two locks.

---

- **防ぐ（ふせぐ）** — to prevent, to defend against, to ward off; transitive verb (他動詞). Used for preventing disasters, crime, or undesirable events. Kango verb. [JLPT N2]

The discovery of penicillin saved many people's lives.

---

- **救う（すくう）** — to save, to rescue, to deliver (from suffering); transitive verb (他動詞). Used for saving lives, souls, or people in dire situations. Wago verb. [JLPT N2]

This machine has the function of removing harmful substances from the air.

---

- **除く（のぞく）** — to remove, to exclude, to eliminate; transitive verb (他動詞). Used for removing physical objects or abstract things (doubts, obstacles). Compound verb 取り除く emphasizes the action of taking away. [JLPT N2]

"Table 1 isn't very relevant, so let's omit it from the materials."

---

- **省く（はぶく）** — to omit, to leave out, to reduce (expenses); transitive verb (他動詞). Similar to 省略する but more concise/wago. The polite sentence frame 〜ましょう suggests a proposal. [JLPT N2]

I made a mistake in driving and caused an accident.

---

- **誤る（あやまる）** — to make a mistake, to err; intransitive verb (自動詞). Note: the transitive sense "to make a mistake in (doing something)" takes a direct object with を. Different from 謝る(あやまる) = to apologize (same pronunciation, different kanji and meaning). [JLPT N2]

A robber entered a convenience store, snatched the sales money from the register, and fled.

---

- **奪う（うばう）** — to snatch, to rob, to take away (by force); transitive verb (他動詞). Used for physical theft or figurative loss (time, attention, life). Wago verb. [JLPT N2]

Now that it's spring, I put away my winter clothes.

---

- **しまう（しまう）** — to put away, to store; transitive verb (他動詞). Also functions as an auxiliary verb (〜てしまう) expressing completion or regret. Here used as the main verb for storing seasonal items. [JLPT N3]

To neglect one's work.

---

- **怠ける（なまける）** — to be lazy, to neglect, to slack off; intransitive verb (自動詞). Derived from 怠る(おこたる) with a more casual nuance. Takes を for the task being neglected. [JLPT N2]

I lost my property in the earthquake.

---

- **失う（うしなう）** — to lose (something abstract: trust, life, opportunity); transitive verb (他動詞). More formal than なくす; used for irreplaceable or significant losses. Wago verb. [JLPT N2]

To attack the enemy.

---

- **攻める（せめる）** — to attack, to assault, to press (someone for answers); transitive verb (他動詞). Used for military attacks, criticism, or aggressive pursuit. Counterpart: 攻められる(せめられる). [JLPT N2]

That student, when reprimanded, glared back at the teacher instead.

---

- **にらむ（睨む）** — to glare at, to stare menacingly; transitive verb (他動詞). Commonly written in kana. Also means "to estimate" or "to keep an eye on" (market trends, suspects). The 逆に adds the nuance of an unexpected reversal. [JLPT N2]

To blame someone for their failure.

---

- **責める（責める）** — to blame, to criticize, to accuse; transitive verb (他動詞). Homophone with 攻める but different kanji and nuance — 責める focuses on verbal/psychological blame, 攻める on physical attack. [JLPT N2]

He betrayed his allies and joined the enemy group.

---

- **裏切る（うらぎる）** — to betray, to go back on (a promise); transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 裏（back/reverse）+ 切る（cut). Implies breaking trust or switching sides. [JLPT N2]

He works to pay his own tuition without relying on his parents.

---

- **頼る（たよる）** — to depend on, to rely on; transitive verb (他動詞). Takes に for the person/thing relied upon. The 〜ず negative form (頼らず) is a literary alternative to 〜ないで. [JLPT N2]

I was in a traffic accident and got injured.

---

- **遭う（あう）** — to encounter (something bad: accident, disaster); intransitive verb (自動詞). Takes に for the event. Different from 会う(あう) = to meet (people), written with different kanji. Used almost exclusively for negative encounters. [JLPT N2]

I invited a friend to my home.

---

- **招く（まねく）** — to invite, to beckon, to lead to (a result); transitive verb (他動詞). Formal/wago. Also used figuratively: 事故を招く (lead to an accident). Note: reading is まねく, not 招(ままねく) as shown — the correct reading is まねく. [JLPT N2]

In the mountains, my clothes caught on a tree and got torn.

---

- **引っ掛かる（引っ掛かる）** — to get caught on, to get stuck; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 引っ掛ける(ひっかける). The ヒット(引っ) prefix intensifies the action. Takes に for what the subject gets caught on. [JLPT N2]

My clothes snagged on a nail and I tore them.

---

- **引っ掛ける（引っ掛ける）** — to snag, to hang (something on), to catch; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 引っ掛かる(ひっかかる). Takes に for the object snagged on. The causal chain (ひっかけて→破ってしまった) shows a sequence of unintended consequences. [JLPT N2]

The boat capsized in the waves and turned completely upside down.

---

- **ひっくり返る（ひっくり返る）** — to turn over, to capsize, to be overturned; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: ひっくり返す(ひっくりかえす). Onomatopoeic prefix ひっくり suggests a complete flipping motion. The sentence adds 上下さかさま as a clarifying explanation. [JLPT N2]

Flip a fish over to grill it.

---

- **ひっくり返す（ひっくり返す）** — to turn over, to flip; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: ひっくり返る(ひっくりかえる). Used for flipping objects (food, cards, furniture). [JLPT N2]

The earthquake caused the railway rails to shift out of alignment.

---

- **ずれる（ずれる）** — to shift, to become misaligned, to deviate; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: ずらす(ずらす). Used for physical displacement (position, schedule) or figurative deviation (from a standard). [JLPT N2]

I moved the desk a little and cleaned the floor.

---

- **ずらす（ずらす）** — to shift, to move out of alignment; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: ずれる(ずれる). Implies a small, intentional adjustment rather than a complete relocation. [JLPT N2]

The mountain collapsed due to heavy rain.

---

- **崩れる（崩れる）** — to collapse, to crumble, to fall apart; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 崩す(くずす). Used for buildings, mountains, or figurative collapse (plans, relationships, market prices). [JLPT N2]

Housing has been built on leveled mountain land.

---

- **崩す（くずす）** — to break down, to level, to demolish; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 崩れる(くずれる). Also used for relaxing one's posture/formality, or breaking apart money (changing a large bill). [JLPT N2]

With a typhoon approaching, both the mountains and the sea are rough.

---

- **荒れる（あれる）** — to become rough, to be wild, to be unsettled; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 荒らす(あらす). Used for weather, sea, land, skin, or one's behavior/room becoming disordered. [JLPT N2]

A burglar broke in and ransacked the room.

---

- **荒らす（あらす）** — to devastate, to ransack, to ruin; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 荒れる(あれる). The adversative passive 荒らされた expresses the speaker's suffering from the burglary. [JLPT N2]

"I acknowledge that this is mine."

---

- **認める（みとめる）** — to recognize, to admit, to acknowledge; transitive verb (他動詞). Kango verb with multiple senses: acknowledge a fact, approve/permit something, or notice/detect. The formal 〜ます frame suits a legal/official declaration. [JLPT N2]

"Double-check before I give you the test."

---

- **見直す（見直す）** — to review, to reconsider, to look again; transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 見（look）+ 直す（redo/correct). The 〜なさい imperative form is a direct command from teacher to student. [JLPT N2]

There's an unfamiliar person in the classroom.

---

- **見慣れる（見慣れる）** — to become accustomed to seeing; intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 見（see）+ 慣れる（get used to). The negative form 見慣れない is commonly used as a pre-modifier: 見慣れない顔 (an unfamiliar face). [JLPT N2]

She is looking for a job.

---

- **求める（もとめる）** — to seek, to desire, to demand; transitive verb (他動詞). Kango verb, more formal than 探す(さがす). Used for abstract goals (employment, truth, approval) as well as concrete objects. [JLPT N2]

Gas is leaking in the kitchen.

---

- **漏れる（もれる）** — to leak, to escape, to come out; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 漏らす(もらす). Used for gas, water, information, or light escaping unintentionally. [JLPT N2]

I carried water in a bucket without spilling a single drop.

---

- **漏らす（もらす）** — to leak (something), to let escape, to spill; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 漏れる(もれる). The expression 一滴も漏らさず (without spilling a single drop) emphasizes carefulness. [JLPT N2]

I planted a fruit-bearing tree in the garden.

---

- **なる（生る／実る）** — to bear fruit, to produce (crops); intransitive verb (自動詞). Different from なる(成る) = to become. Written as 実る when emphasizing ripening. Takes が for what grows and に/で for the location. [JLPT N2]

I overcooked it, and the fish burned completely black.

---

- **焦げる（こげる）** — to burn, to scorch; intransitive verb (自動詞). The subject is the thing that burns (not the person doing the burning). 真っ黒に emphasizes the degree — completely black. The 〜てしまった expresses regret. [JLPT N2]

Contrary to my parents' expectations, I did not go on to university.

---

- **反する（はんする）** — to be contrary to, to go against; intransitive verb (自動詞). Kango suru-verb. Takes に for what is contradicted. Related noun form: 反対(はんたい). The sentence uses the adverbial phrase 期待に反して as a set expression. [JLPT N2]

Rice cakes are puffing up on the wire rack.

---

- **膨れる（ふくれる）** — to swell, to puff up, to bulge; intransitive verb (自動詞). Used for things inflating (cheeks, stomach, tires) or figurative swelling (anger). ほっぺたをふくらます is the transitive counterpart for cheeks. [JLPT N2]

The cherry blossom buds are swelling.

---

- **膨らむ（ふくらむ）** — to swell, to expand, to bulge; intransitive verb (自動詞). Similar to 膨れる but emphasizes gradual expansion or swelling over time. Used for buds, dreams growing, or costs increasing. [JLPT N2]

When my daughter gets angry, she puffs out her cheeks.

---

- **膨らます（ふくらます）** — to puff up, to inflate, to swell (something); transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 膨らむ(ふくらむ). The causative form -ます of 膨らむ. Used for deliberately puffing cheeks, inflating balloons, etc. [JLPT N2]

These shoes have pointed toes.

---

- **とがる（尖る）** — to become pointed, to be sharp; intransitive verb (自動詞). Commonly written in kana. The 〜ている form describes a state (having a pointed shape). Transitive counterpart: 尖らせる(とがらせる). [JLPT N2]

Many lessons from old folk tales still apply to modern times.

---

- **当てはまる（当てはまる）** — to apply, to be applicable, to fit; intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 当て（apply）+ はまる（fit into). Takes に for the target/condition. Counterpart: 当てはめる(あてはめる). [JLPT N2]

After graduating from university, I took up a teaching position.

---

- **就く（就く／つく）** — to assume (a position), to take up (a role); intransitive verb (自動詞). Used for occupations, positions, or seats (職につく, 席につく). Different from 付く (attach) and 着く (arrive) despite same pronunciation. [JLPT N2]

In the club, I was assigned to handle the accounts this year.

---

- **受け持つ（受け持つ）** — to be in charge of, to take responsibility for; transitive verb (他動詞). Compound: 受け（receive）+ 持つ（hold). Used for roles, classes, or responsibilities one takes on. [JLPT N2]

"In case of emergency, please follow the instructions of the staff to evacuate."

---

- **従う（したがう）** — to follow, to obey, to comply with; intransitive verb (自動詞). Takes に for the rule, order, or person followed. Kango verb. Used in formal/official contexts. [JLPT N2]

She was looking down and muttering something to herself.

---

- **つぶやく（呟く）** — to mutter, to mumble, to murmur; intransitive verb (自動詞). The repetition ぶつぶつつぶやいた uses onomatopoeia ぶつぶつ (muttering sound) + the verb, emphasizing the continuous, indistinct quality. [JLPT N2]

To state one's opinion.

---

- **述べる（のべる）** — to state, to express, to describe; transitive verb (他動詞). Kango verb, more formal than 言う. Used for opinions, theories, or accounts. Noun form: 述べる→述べ (statement). [JLPT N2]

In the early morning, I woke up to the sound of birds.

---

- **目覚める（目覚める）** — to wake up, to become conscious, to awaken (to a realization); intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 目（eye）+ 覚める（wake). More vivid/literary than 起きる(おきる). Also figurative: awareness awakening. [JLPT N2]

On the boat, because the passengers shifted to one side, the hull tilted.

---

- **片寄る（偏る／かたよる）** — to be biased, to lean to one side, to be unevenly distributed; intransitive verb (自動詞). The example uses 片寄った for spatial imbalance. 偏る is used for abstract bias (opinions, diet). Counterpart: 偏らせる(かたよらせる). Note: 船体(せんたい) = hull, 傾く(かたむく) = to tilt. [JLPT N2]

The ice melted and the juice became diluted.

---

- **薄まる（薄まる）** — to become thin, to become diluted/weaker; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 薄める(うすめる). Used for concentration, intensity, or color becoming less dense. The ice melting causes the dilution naturally. [JLPT N2]

Add water to dilute the flavor.

---

- **薄める（薄める）** — to dilute, to thin, to weaken; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 薄まる(うすまる). The agent intentionally adds water to reduce concentration. Contrast with 薄まる which is spontaneous. [JLPT N2]

The fog thinned out and visibility improved.

---

- **薄れる（薄れる）** — to fade, to grow thin, to diminish; intransitive verb (自動詞). Similar to 薄まる but emphasizes gradual fading/dissipating. Used for fog, color, memory, or consciousness fading away. [JLPT N2]

The river water is crystal clear.

---

- **透き通る（透き通る）** — to be transparent, to be crystal clear; intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 透き（clear through）+ 通る（pass through). The 〜ている form describes a state. Used for water, glass, or a clear voice. [JLPT N2]

When the teacher entered, the classroom fell completely silent.

---

- **静まる／鎮まる（しずまる）** — to become quiet, to calm down; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 静める(しずめる). [静] refers to 静まる. The onomatopoeia しいんと emphasizes the sudden, complete silence. [JLPT N2]

The moderator silenced the noisy venue with a single word.

---

- **静める／鎮める（しずめる）** — to quiet, to calm, to pacify; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 静まる(しずまる). [静] refers to 静める. The phrase 一言で emphasizes the power and authority of the moderator. [JLPT N2]

He excels in athletic ability.

---

- **優れる（優れる）** — to be excellent, to be superior; intransitive verb (自動詞). Takes が or に for the area of excellence: 運動能力が／に優れている. Used for abilities, qualities, or products being outstanding. [JLPT N2]

"Please don't rush, and speak calmly."

---

- **落ち着く（落ち着く）** — to calm down, to settle down, to become composed; intransitive verb (自動詞). Used for people regaining composure, situations stabilizing, or finding one's place. The 〜て form connects to another command. [JLPT N2]

Work dragged on, and I was late for my appointment.

---

- **長引く（長引く）** — to drag on, to be prolonged; intransitive verb (自動詞). Compound: 長（long）+ 引く（pull/draw). Used for meetings, illnesses, negotiations, or weather lasting longer than expected. [JLPT N2]

As you get older, physical strength declines.

---

- **衰える（衰える）** — to decline, to weaken, to deteriorate; intransitive verb (自動詞). Used for physical strength, memory, skills, or influence gradually diminishing with age or disuse. [JLPT N2]

The Shinkansen is equipped with various safety devices.

---

- **備わる（備わる）** — to be equipped with, to be provided with; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 備える(そなえる). Takes が for what is equipped and に for the location. Indicates natural or inherent possession of features. [JLPT N2]

Fire alarms are installed at the school.

---

- **備える（備える）** — to equip, to provide, to prepare; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 備わる(そなわる). The 〜てある form indicates a deliberate state of preparation. Distinguish: 備わる = naturally/inherently have; 備える = intentionally install/prepare. [JLPT N2]

To accumulate money (to save up).

---

- **蓄える（たくわえる）** — to store, to accumulate, to save up; transitive verb (他動詞). Used for money, supplies, knowledge, or growing out hair/beard. Implies intentional, gradual accumulation. [JLPT N2]

Preparations are in order / are ready.

---

- **整う（整う）** — to be in order, to be ready, to be well-proportioned; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 整える(ととのえる). Takes が for what is ready. Used for preparations, conditions, or features being balanced/neat. [JLPT N2]

Preparations have been made / are complete.

---

- **整える／調える（ととのえる）** — to arrange, to prepare, to adjust, to make neat; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 整う(ととのう). [整] refers to 整える. The を marks the object being prepared (準備). [JLPT N2]

I covered the table with a tablecloth.

---

- **覆う（覆う／おおう）** — to cover, to hide, to conceal; transitive verb (他動詞). Takes を for what is covered and で/で with the covering material. Used for physical covering or abstract concealing (facts, truth). [JLPT N2]

Let's hang out the laundry while the sun is shining.

---

- **照る（照る）** — to shine (of the sun); intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 照らす(てらす). Used specifically for sunlight shining. The 〜ているうちに means "while X is the case" (taking advantage of the condition). [JLPT N2]

I walked along the dark road at night, shining a flashlight at my feet.

---

- **照らす（照らす）** — to illuminate, to shine (light on); transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 照る(てる). Takes を for what is illuminated. Compound noun 夜道(よみち) = night road/dark path. [JLPT N2]

The cloth is dyed with dye.

---

- **染まる（染まる）** — to be dyed, to be colored; intransitive verb (自動詞), counterpart: 染める(そめる). Takes に/で for the dyeing agent and が for what gets dyed. Also figurative: influenced by an environment/culture. [JLPT N2]

Dye cloth with dye.

---

- **染める（染める）** — to dye, to color; transitive verb (他動詞), counterpart: 染まる(そまる). Takes で for the dyeing agent and を for what is dyed. The sentence is a minimal example frame. [JLPT N2]

My eyes are tired, and the text on the screen looks doubled/overlapping.

---

- **ダブる（ダブる／重なる）** — to overlap, to be duplicated, to appear double; intransitive verb (自動詞). From English "double." Commonly written in katakana. The 〜て見える construction expresses visual perception. [JLPT N2]

To admire/yearn for {a professional athlete / a star …}.

---

- **あこがれる（憧れる）** — to long for, to admire, to yearn for; intransitive verb (自動詞). Takes に for the object of admiration. Commonly written in kana. Expresses an aspirational feeling toward an ideal. [JLPT N2]

There's no point in envying other people's happiness.

---

- **うらやむ（羨む）** — to envy, to be jealous of; transitive verb (他動詞). Takes を for what is envied or に for the person envied. The 〜てもしかたがない pattern means "there's no use/point in doing X." [JLPT N2]

I got seriously injured and gave up my dream of becoming a professional soccer player.

---

- **あきらめる（諦める）** — to give up, to abandon, to resign oneself to; transitive verb (他動詞). Takes を for what is given up. Commonly written in kana. Note: not inherently negative — can mean accepting reality gracefully. [JLPT N2]

The new employees know so little that I was dumbfounded.

---

- **あきれる（呆れる）** — to be dumbfounded, to be amazed (at someone's foolishness); intransitive verb (自動詞). Takes に for what causes the amazement. Expresses exasperation or disbelief at something absurd. The 〜ので gives the reason. [JLPT N2]

Animals fear fire.

---

- **恐れる（恐れる／おそれる）** — to fear, to dread, to worry about; transitive verb (他動詞). More formal/literary than 恐がる(こわがる). Takes を for the object of fear. Used in warnings: 〜恐れがある (there is a risk of). [JLPT N2]

Even now, I still harbor resentment toward the classmates who bullied me.

---

- **恨む（恨む／うらむ）** — to resent, to hold a grudge against, to curse; transitive verb (他動詞). Takes を for the target of resentment. Stronger and more lasting than 怒る. The 〜ている form indicates a continuing emotional state. [JLPT N2]

All of us consoled our friend who had gone through a breakup.

---

- **慰める（慰める／なぐさめる）** — to comfort, to console, to cheer up; transitive verb (他動詞). Takes を for the person being comforted. Wago verb. Often used in contexts of grief, disappointment, or emotional pain. [JLPT N2]
